correctness.rationale: With w=sigma^{-(p-1)}, Lerner's mass recurrence gives an anchored A_p sum with ratio 3^{p-1}/2^{2p-1}<1 for every p>1, while R_{1,0} supplies the matching theta^{-(p-1)} lower characteristic. The normalized test sigma 1_Q and the hyperbolic family rs<=D give output p-th power at least c_p theta^{-p} log(1/theta). Reflection costs only a p-dependent constant and product extension preserves the lower bound in all d>=2.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. Lerner's accessible v1 explicitly treats p=2; Ombrosi--Rey's accessible all-p upper-bound paper cites Lerner's lower obstruction specifically at p=2. Exact and synonymous literature searches and the current SCOPE archive did not locate the p!=2 extension or the lower rate A^{1/(p-1)}(log A)^{1/p}. The claim excludes Lerner's recurrence, averaging/reflection devices, and p=2 theorem. Recency leaves residual risk of unindexed simultaneous work.

value.rationale: The theorem shows that failure of the Buckley endpoint power for the strong maximal operator is an all-p phenomenon, not a p=2 accident, and quantifies a logarithmic defect throughout 1<p<infinity and all dimensions d>=2.
